faqs.question: How long does a typical Workflow Automation engagement take?
faqs.answer: Focused automations often ship in 3–8 weeks. Multi-system orchestration programs run longer and are phased by ROI.

faqs.question: Do you work with existing teams and tools?
faqs.answer: Yes. We automate around HubSpot, Zapier, Make, custom APIs, CRMs, ERPs, and internal tools your team already trusts.

faqs.question: How do you measure success?
faqs.answer: Hours saved, error rates, cycle time, SLA adherence, and revenue ops throughput — with before/after baselines.

faqs.question: What processes are good automation candidates?
faqs.answer: Lead routing, onboarding, invoice ops, reporting, ticket triage, enrichment, and any repetitive handoff that burns specialist time.

faqs.question: No-code, low-code, or custom?
faqs.answer: We choose the lightest durable stack. Many flows start in Zapier/Make/HubSpot; complex logic moves to APIs or services when reliability demands it.

faqs.question: How do you handle failures and alerts?
faqs.answer: Retries, dead-letter paths, owner alerts, and runbooks are designed in — silent broken automations are not acceptable.

faqs.question: Will automation replace our team?
faqs.answer: No. We remove busywork so specialists focus on judgment-heavy work. Change management and training are part of delivery.

faqs.question: Can you document everything for our ops team?
faqs.answer: Yes. You get flow diagrams, credentials ownership notes, monitoring checklists, and handover sessions.

faqs.question: How do we get started?
faqs.answer: Pick one painful workflow. We map it, estimate ROI, and pilot a production automation before expanding the roadmap.

faqs.question: Who builds and supports the flows?
faqs.answer: Automation engineers with a delivery lead; optional retainer for monitoring, enhancements, and new workflow backlog.
